help_heading: How companies make it into your strategy
help_intro: You set the rules. Each month, we apply them to the same companies and the same scores for everyone.
help_step_1_text: On the last trading day of each month, we take a snapshot of {total} U.S. companies and their data. Every strategy starts from that same snapshot.
help_step_1_text_sin_cifra: On the last trading day of each month, we take a snapshot of U.S. companies and their data. Every strategy starts from that same snapshot.
help_step_2_text: Sector, size, valuation: whatever you ask for. Companies that fail any rule are excluded, and we can tell you why: “It is worth $1.9B, and you asked for more than $2B.”
help_step_3_text: AI (Jev) scores every company once a month, on four scores. You decide how much each one counts.
help_step_3_extra: If you add your own question, AI answers it only for companies that pass your rules: yes or no, and with what confidence.
help_step_4_text: Your weights produce a score from 0 to 100 for each company. They are ranked, with market capitalization breaking ties. The top N are included. If you set a per-sector limit, it is respected. Anything that does not fill the N slots stays in cash.
help_step_5_title: The portfolio is fixed and compared with the S&P 500
help_step_5_text: The portfolio is fixed with the close of the last trading day of each week. Until half an hour before the market opens on the first trading day of the week you can swap and restore companies; after that it is locked for the week. It is compared with the S&P 500: more than 0.2 points above earns 3 points; within 0.2 points earns 1; below earns 0.

help_fairness_rules: Rules are versioned. Each strategy records which catalog version it played with.
help_fairness_results: Official results are never rewritten. They are fixed when the round closes and stay that way.
help_fairness_scores: Everyone's portfolio is fixed using the same scores. The scores are generated on the afternoon of the month's last trading day, and no one knows how the first day of the week will move when the portfolio is fixed.
help_fairness_house: The house is scored just like you. Alpha, Omega, and Lambda play in the same round, against the same S&P and with the same points; their portfolios come from system methods. The house portfolio is published when the round ends. Everyone sees this week's return.
help_question_text: In your strategy, “Why isn't X included?” tells you whether a company would be included and why. If it still does not add up, write to us.
help_disclaimer: Vennett compares paper strategies: no real money is involved, and this is not financial advice.
